JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 04-08-2022 at about 10-30 p.m. the petitioner as pedestrian, was crossing the road to attend nature call along with one Sri Byresh at B. H road, near Kalpatharu Grand Hotel Gate, Tipturu Town, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7124 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately,
petitioner was shifted to Tipturu Govt Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Siddaganga Hospital, Tumkuru wherein admitted as an inpatient from 05-08-2022 to 14-08-2022.

As per the advice of the doctors, the petitioner has taken treatment as an outpatient on several times by hiring private car on charges of Rs.10,000/- per trip from Tipturu to Tumkuru Siddaganga Hospital.
So far, the petitioner has spent sum of Rs.8,00,000/- towards medical treatment and other incidental charges.
3. Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.

He was working as Police officer (ASI)
at Tipturu Rural Police Station and drawing salary of Rs.55,000/- .

Due to the permanent disability,
he is not in a position to do the said work.
He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability & loss of income.

4. Respondent no.1/the Insurer of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7124 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not holding driving license and the said vehicle was not having Permit and F.C.
as on the date of accident and that the insured vehicle was not at all involved in the accident.
The petitioner in collision with the jurisdictional police have created false record and lodged false complaint, to get compensation.

The respondent no.2 further contended that there is delay of 8 days in lodging the complaint and that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself, as while crossing the road where there was no zebra crossing, he came Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
2 in contact with the unknown vehicle.

sentences.text: 5. Respondent no.2/

the owner of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7124 has filed written statement and contended that he is the RC owner of the car and the said vehicle was insured with the 1st respondent and the police was in force as on the date of accident.

The respondent no.2 further contended that the driver of the said car was driving slowly by observing traffic rules and regulations, but due to the dark night at about 10-30 pm., when a stray dog came in front of the car,
the driver applied the brake to save the dog and lost control over the car and dashed to the petitioner.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries on account of road traffic accident on 04-08- 2022 at about 10-30 pm., near Kalpathru Grand Hotel, Tiptur Town, Tumakuru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.no.KA-41-B-7124 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3
. What Order or Award?
7. The petitioner got examined himself as Pw1 and examined one witness as P.W.2 and marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P14.
The respondent no.2 has examined its Legal Officer as Rw.1 and got marked documents at Ex.R1 and Ex.R2.
Dakshayini -PSI at Chikkanarakanahalli, Tumkuru is examined as RW.2 and Dr Ravi R - Gynecologist at Govt Hospital Tipturu is examined as RW.3.
The respondent no.1 has marked statement given by Byresh on 13-08-2022 as per Ex.R3, during the cross examination of RW.2.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and respondents and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative. Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;
REASONS 10. Issue No.1 : - In order to explain the actionable negligence of the driver of Car bearing Reg.no.KA-41-B- 7124, the P.W.1 has filed his affidavit explaining the vivid picture of the accident Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
3 that took place on 04-08-2022 at about 10-30 p.m. when the petitioner as pedestrian, was crossing the road to attend nature call along with one Sri Byresh at B. H road, near Kalpatharu Grand Hotel Gate, Tipturu Town

, at that time, the driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-B-7124 (herein after called the offending vehicle) came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner,
result of which he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

P.W.1 further deposed about the nature of injuries sustained, treatment taken and the amount spent for treatment etc.
11.

In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 to 9 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Charge sheet, mahazar with sketch, seizure mahazar, IMV report, Notice u/Sec.133 of IMV Act, reply given thereon, 2 photographs relating to the offending vehicle, wound certificate, MLC extract, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Pradeepa B M, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.0141/2022 of Tiptur Town Police Station, for the offence punishable under section 279, 337 of IPC and U/Sec.187 of MV Act.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC and U/Sec.187 of MV Act.
13.

The learned counsel for respondent no.1 has seriously disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and vehemently submitted that the petitioner being the police officials by exercising his power has implicated the offending vehicle in the accident even though the said vehicle was not involved in the accident.

The learned counsel for respondent no.1 has argued much about the delay of 7 days in lodging the complaint and the fact of PW.2 stated to be the eye witness to the accident and stated to be with the petitioner at the time of accident has not shifted the petitioner to the hospital and has not lodged complaint.

It is further argued by the learned counsel for respondent no.1 that there is no evidence as to how the offending vehicle was traced as the vehicle involved in the accident because in the complaint lodged after 7 days of the accident they have not mentioned the vehicle number or the model of the vehicle and that even in the medical records except mentioning history of accident as RTA nowhere has stated the registration number of the vehicle.

It is further argued that in order to prove that PW.2 Byresh was with the petitioner at the time of accident and that they were on the said date and at the said place were on patrolling duty, have not produced Station House Dairy or General Dairy.
It is further argued that there is disproportionate damage on the vehicle when compared to the serious injuries sustained by the petitioner.

It is further argued that the accident in question has occurred near Kalpatharu Grand Hotel, but the investigation officer has not taken steps to collect the CCTV footage from the near by Hotel and mobile tower location was not traced to prove that the accused was driving the vehicle and the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
By seriously disputing the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident, the learned counsel for respondent no.1 has submitted to dismiss the petition.

14. The learned counsel for respondent no.1 during the course of argument has referred the judgment reported in 2010 ACJ 1667 Kar between Bajaja Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. B C Kumar & Anr., wherein the driver pleaded guilty before the criminal court and he was convicted.

sentences.text: It was held that "plea of guilty by the driver cannot be the sole criterion for allowing the claim petition.

sentences.text: In the said case, there was delay of nearly 1 of months in lodging the complaint.
Even though injured was discharged on 28-07-2006 but complaint was lodged by the father of the injured on 06- 08-2006.

On the very day the complaint was lodged, the crime details document surfaced, IMV report was drawn, mahazar as well as sketch map were also drawn the Motor Accident report was drawn on 10-08-2006 and the IMV report does not even mentioned about the vehicle being seized.
The mahazar was drawn in the absence of injured claimant hence it was not made known how and who pointed out the place of accident to the police.
The stand taken by the injured before the Tribunal in his evidence is totally inconsistent with the stand taken by the father in the complaint and other evidence on record.
In the medical records the history of the accident was given as "hit against a road side tree near Bannerghatta Zoo"
Due to the aforesaid reason, the Hon'ble High Court has allowed the appeal preferred by the Insurance company by set aside the order passed by the Tribunal.

15. In (2009) 15 SCC 165 between North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Gourabai & Ors., In the said case, medical evidence showed that deceased suffered injury due to fall in his own house.

entities.text: North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Gourabai & Ors

sentences.text: The brother of the deceased stated he did not know what was written in the document and his signature was taken on it.
It was held doctor will not take a signature on a paper mentioning something in correct.
By relying medical evidence it was held that " injuries sustained were not on account of any vehicular accident.
Hence, dismissed the claim petition.

16. In MFA No. 1519/2007 (WC) between United India Insurance Co.Ltd., Vas. Jali Siddappa &
Anr., In the said case, in the medical evidence the history of injury is given as "due to the hand of the claimant coming under a crushing mixture while he was working with a concrete mixture machine".
The offending vehicle lorry has been brought in to picture at a later stage so as to claim compensation from the Insurance company.
Hence it was observed that injuries sustained by the claimant was not on account of the offending vehicle hitting the claimant and accordingly dismissed the claim petition.

17. In MFA No. 794/2009 between M/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs., Nagamma &
Ors., The documents produced by the claimant, the post morten report evidenced that accident was due to fall from a bicycle.

Ors

sentences.text: The post morten indicated that the death is not as a result of accidental injuries due to involvement of the insured vehicle.
Under the given set of facts, the claim petition was dismissed.
18. Learned counsel for respondent no.1 has referred the judgment reported in ILR 2000 KAR 2009 between Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation Vs. George Ninum.

entities.text: Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation Vs. George Ninum
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said claim petition was filed for damages caused to the vehicle of the petitioner for compensation for the repair of the car.
The said claim petition was rejected on the ground that the claimant has not produced any materials to show that he was the owner of the car.
It was observed that "mere producing document would not sufficient to prove the Special damages.
Such documents have to be proved.

19. The observation made in the aforesaid judgment has no application to the case in hand for the reason that in the said case the claimant having filed petition claiming compensation for repair of the car failed to prove his ownership and failed to prove special damages.

But the present case is for Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
5 claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 20. Coming to the case in hand, it is true that though the accident in question has occurred on 04-08- 2022 but the complaint came to be lodged on 12-08- 2022 ie., after lapse of nearly 7 days from the date of accident.
If the medical records are perused, the petitioner was hospitalized till 14-08-2022.
The complaint was lodged by the son in law of the petitioner.

As per the case of the petitioner , at the time of accident Sri Byresh the police constable of their police station was present and both of them at the time of accident were on patrolling duty and Byresh himself shifted the petitioner to the hospital and he is the eye witness to the accident.

As observed supra, the respondent no.2 has much highlighted the point as to the act of PW.2 stated to be the eye witness has not shifted the injured to the hospital as in the wound certificate the person who accompanied the injured to the hospital is shown as driver of the auto rickshaw but not Byresh.

According to the learned counsel for respondent no.1, if really Byresh was present at the scene of occurrence definitely he would have shifted the injured to the hospital and his name would have been mentioned in the wound certificate as the person brought the injured to the hospital and Byresh would have lodged complaint without any delay and since Byresh was not present he did not lodge the complaint.
21. If the charge sheet is perused, Byresh is cited as an eye witness to the accident.
The petitioner has produced the further statement of Byresh.
The respondent no.1 has marked statement given by Byresh on 13-08-2022 as per Ex.R3.

If Ex.R3 is perused, wherein Byresh has given statement to the effect that Toyota Etios car bearing No. KA-B-7124 was involved in the accident and there is sticker on the rear side of the vehicle with name Kalabairawa.
As per the seizer mahazar the registration number of the vehicle involved in was accident No.KA-41-B-7124 and there is sticker in the said vehicle with name Kalabairawa.

The RW.2 who is the investigation officer has clearly deposed that,
in the night the PW.2 did not notice the registration number of the offending vehicle in accurate and in the statement of PW.2, he has stated the incomplete registration number but the name Kalabairawa in the sticker behind the offending vehicle was correctly mentioned and on the basis of the information given by Byresh regarding the vehicle involved in the accident, they have enquired in the RTO office and ascertained the registration number of the vehicle involved in the accident.

Hence, there is no reason to accept the argument of the learned counsel for respondent no.1 in saying that there is no evidence or materials placed to say how the vehicle involved in the accused was traced out.
So far as non collection of CCTV footage is concerned, it is not brought out from the mouth of the RW.2 that any CCTV was installed near by the commercial premises so as to collect the CCTV footage.

22. So far as the doubt raised regarding the presence of PW.2 at the spot of accident because of his not lodging the complaint and not shifting the injured to the hospital is concerned, the PW.2 and RW.2 have categorically deposed that it is PW.2 being present at the spot has shifted the injured to the hospital in an Auto rickshaw and PW.2 followed the said Auto Rickshaw to the hospital.

Hence,
merely because in the wound certificate, it is mentioned that driver of the Auto rickshaw brought the injured to the hospital the court cannot raise doubt regarding the presence of PW.2 at the spot.

So far as not lodging complaint by PW.2 is concerned, it is clearly stated by PW.2 and it is clearly recited in the complaint that PW.2 informed the fact of accident to the daughter of petitioner over Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
6 phone.

entities.text: Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the PW.2 might throught it not necessary to lodge the complaint as the family members of the petitioner was well informed about the accident .
The medical records as per Ex.P9 discloses that MLC was registered on the date of accident itself at Siddaganga Hospital.

Though RW.3 has deposed that they have given intimation to the jurisdictional PS about the petitioner hospitalized in their hospital on the history of RTA but the RW.2 has categorically deposed that they have not received any intimation from the hospital authority regarding petitioner taking treatment in the hospital on the history of RTA.
Though MLC copy was produced but neither the petitioner nor respondent no.2 has produced the police intimation to prove that intimation was sent to the jurisdictional PS.

When MLC was registered it is the duty of the hospital authority to give intimation to the jurisdictional PS and jurisdictional PS in turn have to visit the hospital and record the statement of the injured if injured is in a position to give the statement or else the statement of the attendant.

Hence, for the fault either of the hospital authority in not giving police intimation or in case if police intimation is given, the fault on the part of the jurisdictional PS in not recording the statement of the injured, for which petitioner cannot be blamed.

So far as the line of argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 regarding non production of Station House dairy, CD etc., to prove the presence of PW.2 at the spot of accident on patrolling duty is concerned,
the very evidence of PW.2, PW.1 and RW.2 would suffice to hold that PW.2 was present at the spot of accident.

23. So far as the observation made in the aforesaid rulings relied by the counsel for respondent no.1 is concerned, it has no application to the case in hand for the reason that in the said case the very occurrence of Road Traffic Accident was not proved leaving apart the involvement of offending vehicle.
But in the present case it is nowhere the case of the respondent no.1 that the petitioner has not sustained injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident.
It is the case of the respondent no.1 that some other vehicle hit the petitioner and caused the accident but not the offending vehicle.
So far as the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.1 regarding much damage not caused to the offending vehicle is concerned
, when offending vehicle hit to the petitioner the question of causing much damage to the offending vehicle does not arise.
If accident was due to the involvement of two vehicle and accident was in between two vehicle then only the damage would be caused to the vehicles.
24. Now at this juncture it would be relevant to refer here the judgment reported in 2023 ACJ 284 between Neha Nilesh Arlekar & Ors., Vs. S D Rocky & Ors.,

entities.text: Neha Nilesh Arlekar & Ors., Vs. S D Rocky & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, motorcycle hit a pedestrian resulting his death.
The Tribunal held that claimants failed to prove involvement of motorcycle and dismissed the claim petition.
Eye witnesses deposed that black coloured motorcycle dashed against the deceased.
It was held merely because police did not record the statement of eye witness or cited him as a witness does not mean that he was not eye witness.
Motorcyclist neither filed written statement nor was he examined.

Mere acquittal of motorcyclist in criminal case does not prove that motorcycle was not involved in the accident as in claim cases issues are required to be proved by the standard of preponderance of probabilities.
25. In 2023 ACJ 661 between Vahida Banu & Ors., Praveen Travels (P) Ltd., & Anr.

In the said case,
pedestrian hit by an unknown bus resulting in his death.
FIR was lodged against unknown person.

A bus driver surrendered before police 5 days after the accident stating that accident was caused by Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
7 him.

entities.text: Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal observed that particulars of bus were not mentioned in the FIR and admission of bus driver 5 days after the accident is doubtful.
In the said case, owner of the bus remained ex-parte.
Insurance company did not examine driver and owner of bus and failed to discharge the burden to prove that the bus was not involved in the accident.
It was held that "Tribunal ought to have taken adverse inference against driver and owner of bus and held that claimants discharge the burden to prove that bus was involved in the accident.

26. The observation made in the aforesaid two judgments relied by the Learned counsel for petitioner is aptly applicable to the case in hand as the owner of the offending vehicle though has filed written statement but has not denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident instead at para no.7 of the written statement has admitted the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident and admitted the offending vehicle hit to the petitioner but taken the defence that on the date of accident it is because stray dog suddenly come in front of the car, the driver of the car suddenly applied break to save the dog and lost control over the car and dashed to the petitioner.
The respondent no.2 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle.

From the documents placed on record it can be gathered that though the offending vehicle was sold in favour of Madhupal Gowda but till the date of accident the RC was not transferred in the name of Madhupal Gowda.
Hence, Chethan who is the RC owner was arrayed as respondent no.2.
At the time of accident Dhanpal Gowda the brother of Madhupal Gowda was driving the offending vehicle.
Hence, charge sheet was filed against Dhanpal Gowda.
The respondent no.1 having disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident has failed to examine the driver of the offending vehicle to substantiate their defence.
Without there being any rebuttal evidence, the court cannot hold that offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
Hence, from the materials placed on record it can be said that offending vehicle was involved in the accident.
27. So far as the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is concerned, if the sketch and spot mahazar is perused,at the time of accident the petitioner was crossing the road.
The accident in question has occurred at about 10-30 pm.,
The offending vehicle which came from Arsikere side in a rash and negligent manner hit to the petitioner who was proceeding on the left side of the road.
Admittedly, complaint was lodged against the driver of the offending vehicle and after investigation charge sheet was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Neither the driver nor owner of the offending vehicle have challenged the charge sheet.
Further nowhere the respondent no.2 in their written statement have stated about the negligence contributed by the petitioner.
Hence, the materials placed on record clearly proves that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, issue no.1 answered in the Affirmative.
28. Issue No.2:-
The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of his sustained grievous injuries.

As observed earlier, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P8 issued from Tipturu Government Hospital to the effect that petitioner has been treated for six injuries of which injury no.1 and 4 are grievous in nature and injury no.2 to 5 and 6 are simple in nature.
29. The discharge summary as per Ex.P.10 issued from Siddaganga Hospital discloses that petitioner has taken treatment from 05-08-2022 to 14-08-2022.
Thus the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for a period of 10 days.

The petitioner has not examined the medical officer Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
8 who has given treatment to him and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability.

entities.text: Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further the petitioner is a Government employee and as per the own evidence of the petitioner, prior to the accident he was drawing monthly salary of Rs.59,000/- and now he is drawing monthly salary of Rs.82,000/.
Hence, there is no loss of income due to the alleged physical disability if any suffered by the petitioner.

Hence, as per the observation made in the judgment relied by the counsel for respondent no.1 reported in ILR 2000 Kar 3443 and ILR 2010 Kar 2439 the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head loss of future income.

The petitioner even not entitled for compensation under the head loss of income during the laid down period, for the reason that the petitioner being a Government Employee is entitled to avail medical leave and also earned leave.
The petitioner has stated that he was under rest for 6 weeks and there is loss of pay for a period of 6 weeks and he is ready to produce document to evidence the said fact.

But the petitioner has failed to produce any document to prove number of days either medical leave or earned leave availed by him and to prove that there was loss of pay during the period of rest taken by him.
30.
Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries and four simple injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
31. Since the petitioner has not produced any medical bills, he is not entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses.
It appears that petitioner has claimed reimbursement of medical expenses from his department, hence, only not produced medical bills.
32. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Siddaganga Hospital.
Further for taking treatment as inpatient in the said hospital he was traveled to hospital for treatment.
He has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.30,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2022.
33. The petitioner at his age of 50 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges

3 . Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 1,00,000/-
 Total Rs. 2,00,000/-

sentences.text:
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only)
34.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with the 1st respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
35. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,01,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh One Thousand only).
A Sum of Rs.2,00,000/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire amount and interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
15. In (2009) 15 SCC 165 between North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation Vs. Gourabai & Ors., In the said case, medical evidence showed that deceased suffered injury due to fall in his own house.
But the present case is for Manjanna Alias Manjanna.K vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38555633/
5 claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
The RW.2 who is the investigation officer has clearly deposed that,
in the night the PW.2 did not notice the registration number of the offending vehicle in accurate and in the statement of PW.2, he has stated the incomplete registration number but the name Kalabairawa in the sticker behind the offending vehicle was correctly mentioned and on the basis of the information given by Byresh regarding the vehicle involved in the accident, they have enquired in the RTO office and ascertained the registration number of the vehicle involved in the accident.
So far as non collection of CCTV footage is concerned, it is not brought out from the mouth of the RW.2 that any CCTV was installed near by the commercial premises so as to collect the CCTV footage.
Hence,
merely because in the wound certificate, it is mentioned that driver of the Auto rickshaw brought the injured to the hospital the court cannot raise doubt regarding the presence of PW.2 at the spot.
Though MLC copy was produced but neither the petitioner nor respondent no.2 has produced the police intimation to prove that intimation was sent to the jurisdictional PS.
When MLC was registered it is the duty of the hospital authority to give intimation to the jurisdictional PS and jurisdictional PS in turn have to visit the hospital and record the statement of the injured if injured is in a position to give the statement or else the statement of the attendant.
Hence, for the fault either of the hospital authority in not giving police intimation or in case if police intimation is given, the fault on the part of the jurisdictional PS in not recording the statement of the injured, for which petitioner cannot be blamed.
But in the present case it is nowhere the case of the respondent no.1 that the petitioner has not sustained injuries due to the Road Traffic Accident.
It is the case of the respondent no.1 that some other vehicle hit the petitioner and caused the accident but not the offending vehicle.
, when offending vehicle hit to the petitioner the question of causing much damage to the offending vehicle does not arise.
If accident was due to the involvement of two vehicle and accident was in between two vehicle then only the damage would be caused to the vehicles.
Mere acquittal of motorcyclist in criminal case does not prove that motorcycle was not involved in the accident as in claim cases issues are required to be proved by the standard of preponderance of probabilities.
25. In 2023 ACJ 661 between Vahida Banu & Ors., Praveen Travels (P) Ltd., & Anr.
The respondent no.2 is the RC owner of the offending vehicle.
From the documents placed on record it can be gathered that though the offending vehicle was sold in favour of Madhupal Gowda but till the date of accident the RC was not transferred in the name of Madhupal Gowda.
At the time of accident Dhanpal Gowda the brother of Madhupal Gowda was driving the offending vehicle.
Hence, charge sheet was filed against Dhanpal Gowda.
The respondent no.1 having disputed the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident has failed to examine the driver of the offending vehicle to substantiate their defence.
Without there being any rebuttal evidence, the court cannot hold that offending vehicle was not involved in the accident.
The petitioner even not entitled for compensation under the head loss of income during the laid down period, for the reason that the petitioner being a Government Employee is entitled to avail medical leave and also earned leave.
But the petitioner has failed to produce any document to prove number of days either medical leave or earned leave availed by him and to prove that there was loss of pay during the period of rest taken by him.
30.
Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained two grievous injuries and four simple injuries.
Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.
31. Since the petitioner has not produced any medical bills, he is not entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.1,00,000/-.
Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-
 2. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 30,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges
3 . Loss of discomfort and amenities Rs. 1,00,000/-
 Total Rs. 2,00,000/-
Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh only)
34.
Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 1 this court directs the respondent no.1 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
35. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- + cost of Rs.1,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,01,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh One Thousand only).
A Sum of Rs.2,00,000/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire amount and interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
